rounds.text: Akanksha Power & Infrastructure Ltd is experiencing a powerful acceleration in its business fundamentals, highlighted by compounded sales growth surging to 23% over 3 years and compounded profit growth reaching 25% over the same period [E9, E12]. Recent performance is even more striking, with trailing twelve-month profit growth hitting 31% and screens noting net profit up by 73% year-over-year [E13, E47]. This fundamental turnaround is paired with significant operational efficiency gains, demonstrated by debtor days dramatically improving from 158 to 94.3 days and working capital requirements contracting from 91.5 days to just 35.6 days [E40, E41]. Furthermore, cash generation is robust, featuring an exceptional cash conversion ratio of 2.19x where operating cash flows of Rs 12.53 Cr fully backed reported profits at 129% of operating profit in March 2026 [E22, E23, E25]. Operating margins are also expanding, moving up to 13% in March 2026 and reaching 14% quarterly, outperforming the company's historical levels and demonstrating stronger pricing or cost execution [E18, E19]. conceded: [E34], [E36], [E43].

While the bull points to 3-year compounded sales growth of 23% and profit growth of 25% [E9, E12], these numbers mask a severe long-term growth slowdown, evidenced by a dismal 5-year sales growth rate of just 3% [E8]. Conceded: [E13], [E47]. Although the bull highlights working capital improvements and cash generation metrics [E40, E41, E22, E23, E25], it ignores the negative free cash flow of Rs -18.99 Cr in March 2026 [E24] and a sharp surge in total borrowings to Rs 42.95 Cr from Rs 26.77 Cr a year prior [E28]. Furthermore, the cited margin expansions to 13% and 14% [E18, E19] are undermined by the company's inconsistent yearly and quarterly operating-margin trends [E20, E21], proving that recent gains lack structural stability. Finally, the bullish narrative of an accelerating business completely overlooks the reality that the stock price has fallen 14% over the past year [E14], institutional confidence has vanished with foreign and domestic institutional holdings dropping to absolute zero [E31, E32], and the current valuation prices in an aggressive 13.0% earnings growth that vastly exceeds the 8.0% base case [E36].
